subject: MAP: BlueHorizon capacity handoff & evaluation schedule
messages:
From: Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwood.ai>
To: Sarah Miller <sarah.miller@bluehorizon.ai>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Date: 2027-04-04T09:15:00-07:00
Subject: MAP: BlueHorizon capacity handoff & evaluation schedule

Sarah — great to meet last week. Per our conversation I pulled together a first-pass Mutual Action Plan (attached) focused on capacity reservation for Dedicated + Private. Goal here: a clear path from eval to commit that balances lead times, acceptance criteria, and a fallback if hardware delivery slips.

High-level asks from BlueHorizon I captured:
- 8-week evaluation window on a dedicated 2-GPU staging cluster (H100-equivalent perf target)
- Production target: 12 GPU pool (mix of A100/H100), 24/7 traffic, regional isolation in us-west
- SOC2 evidence and audit logs required before cutover

From our side, main gating items:
- Procurement lead time for dedicated tranche (8–12 weeks after signed commit depending on SKU and region)
- Acceptance runbook and perf sign-off during week 6 of eval
- Canary: 2-week staged ramp before full cutover

Next steps I propose this week:
1) You confirm the evaluation KPI deck attached to the MAP (latency p50/p95, throughput targets, quality knobs)
2) We schedule a 45-min technical sync (Ben + infra) to validate the sizing assumptions on Wed or Thu
3) Procurement point-of-contact so we can align on purchase order cadence and billing terms

Attaching: bluehorizon_map_v1.xlsx (MAP + milestones).

Thanks — want to make this as prescriptive and low-friction as possible.

— Naomi
Naomi Feldman
Head of GTM, Redwood Inference
naomi.feldman@redwood.ai
+1 (415) 555-0142

From: Sarah Miller <sarah.miller@bluehorizon.ai>
To: Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwood.ai>
Cc: procurement@bluehorizon.ai
Date: 2027-04-05T11:03:00-07:00
Subject: Re: MAP: BlueHorizon capacity handoff & evaluation schedule

Thanks Naomi — reviewed and helpful. A couple of clarifying notes from procurement and the platform team:

Procurement: PO window is tight for Q3 budget; if we sign by May 10 we can include this under our current procurement authorization. Billing preference is monthly committed with quarterly reconciliation.

Platform notes (from our infra lead): we can provision a staging cluster with equivalent memory/FP performance but would prefer a 3-node staging (to validate sharding/failure modes) vs 2-node. That would change the eval footprint slightly.

Questions:
1) Can Redwood compress the procurement lead time if we accept a mixed tranche (3x reserved + 9x on-burst) to start?
2) What are the acceptance test scripts you want running during week 6? Can you share a checklist?

I'll loop in Jules from legal after we align on MAP dates.

- Sarah
Sarah Miller
Senior Program Manager, BlueHorizon Diagnostics
sarah.miller@bluehorizon.ai
From: Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwood.ai>
To: Sarah Miller <sarah.miller@bluehorizon.ai>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwood.ai>
Date: 2027-04-06T08:20:00-07:00
Subject: Re: MAP: BlueHorizon capacity handoff & evaluation schedule

Appreciate the quick review, Sarah — answers inline and updated a couple of rows in the MAP tab.

1) Mixed tranche option: yes, we can offer a 3 reserved + 9 burst starter. Tradeoffs: reduces procurement lead time to ~4–6 weeks for the reserved tranche (we can convert burst -> reserved on the same pool later) but unit cost will be slightly higher during the first 90 days. We include clear flagging in the MAP so BlueHorizon can choose the commit path at signature.

2) Acceptance scripts: attaching technical_sizing_v2.pdf. Key items we run during week 6:
   - Perf: p50/p95 latency at target QPS with KV cache warmed and real prefix traces
   - Throughput: sustained tokens/sec for 2-hour soak at expected corpus mix
   - Correctness: sample prompt sets for clinical extraction tasks (quality thresholds must be met)
   - Failure modes: node kill/restart, network flake simulation, and cold-start latency profiles

Ben — can you confirm the staging sizing (3-node) and whether the canary timeline needs adjustment? Priyom — can you add a short note on rollback and fallback model variants to the MAP?

Naomi

Attachment: technical_sizing_v2.pdf
From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
To: Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwood.ai>, Sarah Miller <sarah.miller@bluehorizon.ai>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Date: 2027-04-07T10:56:00-07:00
Subject: Re: MAP: BlueHorizon capacity handoff & evaluation schedule

Quick technical readout:
- Staging: agree with 3-node H100-equivalent; that gives us realistic shard distribution and KV cache behavior. We'll provision with 2x 80GB + 1x 40GB to simulate heterogeneous pool behavior.
- Prod sizing: baseline 12 GPUs as discussed (mix: 6x H100, 6x A100) — we recommend starting with 8 hot-capacity and 4 burstable to reduce upfront spend.
- Lead-time: for H100 reservations in us-west, plan on 9 weeks if we go full reserved. For the mixed tranche Naomi proposed, we can get the 3 reserved nodes in ~5 weeks and enable burst expansion immediately.

Canary/rollback: Plan 2-week canary with throttled traffic (10% -> 40% -> 75% -> 100%). In the event of perf regression, automatic fallback to the Redwood-hosted lighter model variant is in the MAP.

I'll add sizing sheet rows and a small runbook snippet to the shared MAP (technical_sizing_v2.pdf).

— Ben
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
To: Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>, Sarah Miller <sarah.miller@bluehorizon.ai>

Date: 2027-04-09T09:08:00-07:00
Subject: Re: MAP: BlueHorizon capacity handoff & evaluation schedule

Thanks team — added operational acceptance items in the MAP under "Onboarding & SLA gates":
- Audit logs: 30-day retention for initial rollout, 1-year optional add-on (SOC2 evidence folder link included)
- Runbook handoff checklist: SRE on-call, escalation matrix, maintenance windows, model rollout policy
- Cost guardrails: per-route throttles + token budget alerts for first 90 days

Also noted a go/no-go checkpoint at day 42 (end of week 6) after running the acceptance scripts. If BlueHorizon requests earlier conversion, we can offer a soft-convert (billing switches) with a 2-week extended canary.

I've attached the updated MAP with those rows: bluehorizon_map_v1.xlsx (v1.1).

— Marissa
Director, Customer Success, Redwood Inference
From: Jules R. <jules@bhlegal.com>

Date: 2027-04-11T16:42:00-07:00
Subject: Re: MAP: BlueHorizon capacity handoff & evaluation schedule — contract redlines

Naomi / team — attaching our redlines and a short summary: main ask is a 45-day termination-for-convenience clause during the initial 90-day evaluation and a data-retention SLA aligned with HIPAA controls (BlueHorizon is regulated). We flagged indemnity language and request a limited liability cap tied to fees for the first year.

If Redwood can accept the mixed tranche and the 45-day early-termination carve-out, we can push to sign by May 6 and hit procurement timelines. Attached: contract_redline_BH.docx

Jules
Legal Counsel, BlueHorizon Diagnostics
